label: GO step, agent choosing a1, late in episode (trial >= ~50)
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (never at D1 or D2) when the agent itself selects a1 (model_act == 1; 93% of activation mass), and only late in the episode: it is silent for trials 0-29 and its firing rate climbs steadily from trial ~30 to trial ~80. The predicate uses only the agent own current policy output and the episode position, which the agent can track, so no future variable is involved. Activation rate is highest when the a1 logit margin is largest (choice > 8: 45% rate, 67% of mass). The top activation quartile is 98% covered by the predicate; the misses are weak activations on a2 choices or on trials 40-49. It does not depend on the previous reward, the transition type, stay/switch or core pattern (all about 1.0x lift), and it is absent at the highest-value steps (value > 8.1). False positives are late a1 GO steps where it stays silent, often during long rewarded a1 streaks; a value cutoff did not improve on this. It is an a1-choice x late-episode conjunction, so explanation is partial (dev F1 0.78, mass recall 0.91).
